cards.body: NVIDIA is expanding its family of open models across language, robotics, biology, and quantum computing, giving developers, researchers and enterprises what they need to build applications tailored to local languages and industries The portfolio includes the new NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt models; new NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever models for embedding, reranking and document parsing; the new NVIDIA Kumo family open weight foundation models and libraries for structured business data; NVIDIA Cosmos 3.5 world models; NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Edge for autonomous vehicles; NVIDIA BioNeMo for healthcare and scientific discovery; and NVIDIA Ising for quantum computing. The open models give organizations a foundation they can customize with local data and deploy on infrastructure they control. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements NVIDIA Nemotron Powers Post-Training Across Industries NVIDIA Nemotron brings open language models, datasets and recipes to developers building agents. The models support text and images, helping agents orchestrate workflows, reason through complex problems and complete specialized tasks at a lower cost. Nemotron models are built with data, research and expertise from the NVIDIA Nemotron Coalition , including European partners Black Forest Labs , H-Company and Mistral . Nemotron provides a foundation for enterprises to build applications based on their own knowledge and expertise. Dassault Systèmes , Domyn , Dream , Palantir’s customers , Salesforce , SAP , Shopify , Synopsys and WPP , as well as professional services providers like Accenture and EY, are working with Nemotron models and datasets to create custom models and build domain-specific agents. A broad ecosystem of post-training partners, including AfterQuery , AgileRL , AI21 , Alice , Applied Compute , Baseten , CoreWeave , Distil Labs , EON , Fastino , Fireworks , Google Cloud, Mercor , Multiverse Computing , Nebius , Handshake AI , Plurai , Prime Intellect , River.AI, Scale AI , Trajectory and TNG, is helping enterprises customize Nemotron for domain-specific workloads. NVIDIA Kumo Speeds Agents’ Work With Structured Enterprise Data NVIDIA Kumo open foundation models, libraries and tools help agents and applications forecast outcomes, score fraud risk and recommend actions from structured business data. Part of NVIDIA Agent Knowledge Foundation , Kumo shortens time to prediction and reduces the cost and complexity of building a separate machine learning pipeline for every task. Developers can use pretrained Kumo models to bring predictions to more applications quickly, then fine-tune them using proprietary data when higher performance is critical. The portfolio includes NVIDIA Kumo Structured , with models for relational and tabular prediction, forecasting and anomaly detection, and NVIDIA Kumo Engine , an open library stack for developing and deploying structured data foundation models. summary_data.subject_angle: NVIDIA는 칩(Jetson Thor) 공급을 넘어 **GR00T 파운데이션 모델, 시뮬레이션(Isaac Lab, Cosmos), 런타임(Isaac OS), 안전 스택(Halos)까지 수직 통합한 풀스택 로보틱스 플랫폼 기업**으로 포지셔닝을 강화하고 있으며, 이는 데이터센터 중심 AI 사업을 물리적 AI(피지컬 AI)로 확장하는 전략의 핵심 축이다.
summary_data.focus_angle: **Jetson Thor와 GR00T를 탑재한 레퍼런스 휴머노이드가 2027년 초 등장**함으로써 완성형 휴머노이드 OEM과 연구기관들이 자체 하드웨어·AI 스택 개발 없이도 NVIDIA 표준을 채택할 길이 열리며, 이는 자율주행·산업 로봇 OEM들에게도 **시뮬레이션-실세계 전이(Isaac Lab, Cosmos 기반 합성 데이터)를 통한 개발 주기 단축**이라는 레퍼런스 모델을 제시한다.

cards.body: News Summary: - Agile Robots announces Agile ONE SN, a humanoid reference platform built on NVIDIA Isaac GR00T and NVIDIA Jetson Thor with planned integration of the NVIDIA Halos safety stack, giving developers and researchers a complete platform for frontier humanoid development and validation. - NVIDIA Isaac platform adds new Isaac OS runtime, Isaac Lab 3.0 for robot learning and open source reference workflows that combine ChatGPT Astra with NVIDIA Isaac and Cosmos on NVIDIA DGX Station to accelerate robot data generation, training and evaluation. - Europe’s robotics ecosystem, including leaders like ABB Robotics, Flexion, Hexagon Robotics, Humanoid, KUKA, NEURA Robotics, Sereact and Universal Robots, is building on NVIDIA’s open robotics platform to advance autonomous robotic systems. GTC Berlin—NVIDIA today announced a major expansion of the NVIDIA Isaac™ open robotics development platform, adding a reference humanoid, datasets and runtime, along with updates to its robot learning framework. Together, these technologies give developers an integrated path from data to deployment to bring general-purpose robots to the real-world faster. “General-purpose robotics is advancing at extraordinary speed — the ChatGPT moment for robotics is fast approaching,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “With NVIDIA Isaac, our full-stack open robotics platform, we are giving developers the models, data, simulation tools and computing systems to bring physical AI to the world’s largest industries.” Agile ONE SN — A Frontier Humanoid Reference Platform for Research Agile Robots announced Agile ONE SN, a full-stack reference humanoid preconfigured with NVIDIA Isaac GR00T and powered by the NVIDIA Jetson Thor™ edge AI platform. Robotics researchers and developers often struggle to integrate the separate simulation, training and deployment tools needed to take robot skills from development to the physical world. Agile ONE SN unifies these tools and workflows on a single platform, cutting setup time from weeks to days. cards.body: News Summary: - NVIDIA introduces DSX POD, a reference design for complete Vera Rubin AI factories built by partners in modular containers, integrated and validated before delivery. - Factory-built units reduce deployment time at a prepared site from six months to as little as 14 days, helping customers begin generating production tokens and earning revenue sooner. - A global ecosystem of computing and infrastructure partners are working with NVIDIA to deliver modular AI factories worldwide in early 2027. GTC Berlin—NVIDIA today introduced DSX POD, a reference design for complete NVIDIA Vera Rubin AI factories built by partners inside modular containers, integrated and validated before delivery. The units arrive ready to connect out of the box to a prepared site’s power, cooling, networking and other supporting infrastructure, reducing deployment time from six months to as little as 14 days. DSX POD moves the integration and installation of computing, networking, cabling, rack-level power and liquid cooling to the manufacturing facility, reducing the extensive planning, construction, specialized labor and logistics of a traditional onsite build. Factory-tested containers reduce exposure to component delays and costly, error-prone onsite work, creating a shorter path to model training and production inference so customers can begin generating tokens and earning revenue sooner. “An AI factory creates value when it starts producing tokens — not when construction is complete,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “With NVIDIA DSX POD, we’re bringing factory-built precision and speed to AI infrastructure construction — reducing deployment time from months to weeks so customers can scale capacity and bring revenue-generating production online faster.” Factory-Built Infrastructure NVIDIA DSX POD brings Vera Rubin systems together with the infrastructure needed to operate them in repeatable, factory-built, containerized designs that partners can manufacture and deliver at scale. It carries forward the design philosophy of the broader NVIDIA DSX™ infrastructure platform, with a distinct architecture that integrates and validates systems in purpose-built containers before transport and deployment. Partners complete rack-to-rack cabling, wiring, piping and functional validation before shipment. This work takes place separately from site preparation, further shortening the time needed to bring new capacity online. That earlier start to production is the link between deployment speed and economics. Time to first token marks when a new AI factory begins running models to serve production workloads, giving operators the opportunity to put their infrastructure to work for customers sooner. key_facts: DSX Pod는 **Vera Rubin NVL72 기반 7개 액체냉각 컴퓨트 랙을 17km Spectrum X 케이블로 연결**, 공장에서 완전 조립·배선·테스트 후 컨테이너로 운송
건식 냉각(dry cooling)과 800V DC 전력 공급 방식 채택
Huang은 설치~토큰 생산까지 시간을 **4~5개월에서 약 1개월로 단축** 가능하다고 주장, 1GW 데이터센터는 약 $50B 비용에 $40B 매출 기대, 3개월 지연 시 $10B 매출 손실
휴머노이드 레퍼런스 로봇 **Agile One SN은 1.4m 신장, 5지 손가락, 2,070 FP4 테라플롭스, 128GB 통합 메모리**를 탑재하며 내년 1분기 사전조립 상태로 출시 예정
Amkor Technology, IBIDEN, King Yuan Electronics(KYEC), Samsung Electro-Mechanics, SPIL, Unimicron과 공급망 파트너십 체결, 반도체 테스트 용량은 2026년 대비 2027년 2배 확대 목표
summary_data.why_matters: NVIDIA는 단순 칩 공급자를 넘어 **데이터센터 구축의 병목(전기기사 부족, 배선·조립 지연)까지 해결하는 풀스택 공급업체**로 포지셔닝을 확장하고 있다. 동시에 휴머노이드 로봇과 반도체 후공정(패키징·테스트·광학엔진) 공급망까지 수직 확장함으로써 AI 인프라 전반에 대한 통제력을 강화하고 있다.
summary_data.subject_angle: DSX Pod는 **NVIDIA가 하드웨어 설계뿐 아니라 데이터센터 구축·운영 속도까지 제품화**함으로써 하이퍼스케일러와 뉴트럴 클라우드(neocloud) 고객의 ROI(매출 지연 리스크)를 직접 겨냥한 전략으로 해석된다. Samsung Electro-Mechanics, SPIL 등 후공정 파트너 확대는 TSMC 의존도를 낮추고 CPO(co-packaged optics) 생산능력을 선제적으로 확보하려는 움직임이다.
summary_data.focus_angle: 휴머노이드 레퍼런스 로봇 **Agile One SN**은 NVIDIA Isaac 플랫폼이 소프트웨어·레퍼런스 설계를 넘어 완제품에 가까운 형태로 로보틱스 생태계 표준화를 시도하는 사례로, 자동차·물류·제조 현장의 휴머노이드 로봇 상용화 경쟁에 직접적인 영향을 줄 수 있다.

cards.body: CONTROL Huang shrugs off protestors to kick off GTC Berlin with DSX Pods, Robots GTC Jensen Huang kicked off GTC Europe by promising to cut the time to token at new datacenters from months to weeks, with a Vera Rubin-powered AI factory in a box. The DSX Pod – essentially a containerized version of its DSX reference architecture – was the hardware highlight of the Nvidia CEO and founder’s keynote speech, which was much about assuring Europe that it had a future in the AI era and namechecking the vendor’s key partners such as Schneider Electric and Siemens Electric, as unveiling brand new tech. Huang described the Pod as “bringing this full-stack platform into a factory-built integrated system.” According to a video it “starts with Vera Rubin NVL72. Seven liquid-cooled compute racks connected with 17 kilometers of Spectrum X cables form a Vera Rubin DSX pod. Vera Rubin DSX pods are integrated, fully cabled, and factory tested, then delivered in transportable containers.” The design relies on dry cooling rather than traditional evaporative cooling, and 800V DC for “efficient power delivery.” None of that is new in itself – they’re part of the standard DSX architecture. But NVIDIA is targeting the deployment and supply chain challenges facing datacenter operators. “The scale at which we are now producing computing is unheard of ever. Unimaginable,” said Huang. “Well, even then, when you bring these systems onto your sites, there are still months and months of assembly, and you just heard 17,000 kilometers of wiring to connect just Spectrum X for the scale-out computing. It’s a crazy number.” That’s why buildouts such as TeraWulf’s Lake Mariner site outside Buffalo New York run into shortages of electricians before they have to deal with shortages of GPUs and DRAM. Nearly half of the 1,800 trades on site are electricians. But, said Huang, “Now suppose we were to do that all inside the supply chain, run everything up, build everything up, make sure that it runs completely, get it qualified, burnt in, and by the time we ship it, it is fully functional. The amount of cabling and on-site assembly is going to be greatly reduced.” But, just as importantly, he said, “By moving this into the supply chain the amount of idle computing, the amount of idle computing that's going to be sitting inside at your datacenters will reduce dramatically.” Afterall, he said, a 1GW datacenter costs about $50 billion, with operators expecting to generate revenues of $40bn off the back of that infrastructure. headlines.body: News Summary: - Substrate agreements with IBIDEN, Samsung Electro-Mechanics and Unimicron Technology Corporation will, in aggregate, drive a 2.5x increase in capacity over the next three years. - Amkor plans to increase its advanced packaging capacity by more than 300% by the end of 2028. - KYEC will build new facilities in the U.S., supported by a $1.1 billion capacity reservation advance from NVIDIA. - SPIL is targeting to increase its optical-engine capacity for co-packaged optics by 15x by mid-2027, with aims for another doubling by the end of 2028. GTC Berlin—NVIDIA today announced plans with a group of supply chain partners to expand global manufacturing capacity to meet growing demand for its accelerated computing and full-stack AI factory platform. Working with Amkor Technology, IBIDEN, King Yuan Electronics (KYEC), Samsung Electro-Mechanics, Siliconware Precision Industries (SPIL) and Unimicron Technology Corporation, NVIDIA is enabling new and existing suppliers to expand critical manufacturing capabilities across substrates, advanced packaging, testing and optical engines, strengthening the resiliency and redundancy of NVIDIA’s global supply chain. “We are in the midst of the largest infrastructure buildout in human history. Demand is extraordinary. Capacity is the constraint,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “Our supply chain partners are the world’s best manufacturers. I’m grateful they are expanding capacity around the globe to scale production and help us deliver the AI supercomputing systems powering this new industrial revolution.” Expanding Substrate Capacity to Support Volume Growth NVIDIA plans to increase substrate capacity for its products by 2.5x over the next three years. The agreements below will contribute to this capacity expansion, with more underway. Under an agreement signed and announced earlier this year by IBIDEN, NVIDIA is providing a multibillion-dollar capacity reservation advance to support IBIDEN’s Ono Plant in Japan. The expansion targets capacity reaching 3x current levels at the plant, with additional capacity expected to begin ramping in the first quarter of 2028. Samsung Electro-Mechanics is joining NVIDIA’s substrate supply chain, bringing immediate capacity from its existing operations in South Korea. The collaboration also supports facility upgrades and new factories in Sejong and Busan, South Korea. By 2028, production allocated to NVIDIA is projected to account for a significant portion of Samsung Electro-Mechanics’ total annual package substrate production capacity. NVIDIA is supporting Unimicron’s KF substrate manufacturing expansion in Taiwan with a capacity reservation agreement. The expansion is expected to begin adding capacity in the second quarter of 2027 and reach full capacity by mid-2028. headlines.body: General availability of the instances is coming next month, with planned expansion of availability to Europe — bringing an integrated platform for training, inference and large-scale reinforcement learning to cloud customers. A5X instances bring together NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72, NVIDIA ConnectX-9 SuperNICs, Google Cloud Virgo Network and Google Cloud’s fourth-generation advanced liquid-cooling technology for demanding agentic inference and reinforcement learning workloads at scale. Google Cloud plans to scale its Vera Rubin-based infrastructure to as many as 960,000 Rubin GPUs across multiple sites. Ineffable Intelligence , a London-based technology company founded by AlphaGo creator David Silver, was the first customer to access A5X. Ineffable is using the platform to advance large-scale reinforcement learning and shape “superlearner” systems that learn continuously from experience. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Learning through interaction requires a continuous cycle of generating experience, evaluating outcomes and updating models, requiring infrastructure that can support the entire process at scale. A5X brings Vera Rubin into Google Cloud’s AI Hypercomputer as an integrated system, combining compute, networking and storage to support experience-driven learning at scale. “We’re building superlearners that continually improve through their own experience,” said David Silver, founder and CEO of Ineffable Intelligence. “That demands both substantial compute and a tight connection between generating experience and training on it, so each improvement in the agent can quickly shape its next experience. Vera Rubin’s combination of compute performance and high-bandwidth connectivity, between the Vera CPU and Rubin GPUs and between the Rubin GPUs within the rack, allow us to push the scale and ambition of our reinforcement learning research further.” WPP , a London-based marketing and communications company, has also demonstrated its creative agent reference architecture on NVIDIA Vera Rubin-based A5X instances using NVIDIA Nemotron models and NVIDIA OpenShell, part of the NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture for safe AI agents. The agents turn conversational requests into multistep creative workflows, such as video generation, upscaling and restyling, with human approval before execution. OpenShell provides governed sandboxes for agent execution, helping control access to sensitive brand assets and creative tools. In WPP’s initial tests, workloads that typically required a multi-node cluster ran on a single A5X instance. As organizations deploy agentic systems, they need to protect the proprietary models and sensitive data that power these systems — even when running on infrastructure they don’t own. headlines.body: News Summary: - The NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture delivers enterprise governance, isolation and security for building, containing, observing and enforcing safe agents across enterprise infrastructure and edge systems. - Built on the foundation of NVIDIA OpenShell secure runtime software, the architecture brings together NVIDIA Vera Rubin infrastructure for model inference, NVIDIA Vera CPUs for agent harnesses and tool use, and NVIDIA BlueField-4 DPUs running NVIDIA Sentry for in-silicon enforcement. The OpenShell Reference Architecture extends to the edge with NVIDIA RTX Spark, NVIDIA DGX Spark and NVIDIA DGX Station systems. - The OpenShell Reference Architecture runs on leading enterprise operating systems, including Canonical, Red Hat, and Microsoft Windows and Microsoft Execution Containers. - Anthropic, AWS, Cisco, CrowdStrike, Dassault Systèmes, Dell Technologies, Google Cloud, HPE, IBM, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, Palo Alto Networks, Perplexity, SAP, ServiceNow, Siemens, SpaceX Super Intelligence and others are among those working with the OpenShell Reference Architecture to enhance the security of agent deployments. GTC Berlin—NVIDIA today announced the NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture, which enables building, containing, observing and enforcing safe agents on enterprise infrastructure and edge systems. The OpenShell Reference Architecture builds on the foundation of NVIDIA OpenShell™ secure runtime software, extending it into full-stack, industrial-scale infrastructure for agent development and operations. It includes NVIDIA Vera Rubin infrastructure for running enterprise workloads, including closed and open models built with NVIDIA Nemotron™; NVIDIA Vera CPUs for operating agent harnesses; open source NVIDIA OpenShell software; and NVIDIA BlueField® DPUs for running the NVIDIA Sentry unified security software framework that provides continuous out-of-band monitoring of agent behavior and in-silicon policy enforcement. The OpenShell Reference Architecture is extensible to agents running at the edge across industries such as retail, healthcare, manufacturing, robotics, software development and telecommunications with NVIDIA RTX Spark™, NVIDIA DGX Spark™ and NVIDIA DGX Station™ systems. “AI capability and safety must advance together,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “As enterprises prepare to deploy billions of AI agents, safety and control must be built into the computing architecture. Leading enterprises are using the open source NVIDIA Agent Toolkit — now expanded with new tools — to customize and control agents, use company data to inform their answers and actions, monitor what they do and govern how they operate. NVIDIA Agent Knowledge Foundation helps enterprises turn data into company intelligence agents can use. Agents can find relevant information, understand what it means for the business and use it to make predictions and help people decide what to do next. Companies can use Agent Knowledge Foundation without moving data, rebuilding existing workflows or changing governance controls. The foundation features NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries , including cuDF, cuGraph, cuML, cuOpt and cuVS, and the new Auto-Ontology library, which translates raw company data into familiar business concepts — like customers, products and orders — and maps how they relate. OpenShell provides the secure runtime boundary, giving enterprises control over what agents can access and do. NVIDIA NemoClaw blueprints provide reference designs for building secure, specialized agents. The newest NemoClaw blueprint for agent optimization provides a step-by-step starting point for improving agent intelligence — making them better at their jobs over time. related.title: Nvidia announces plug and play Vera Rubin racks that can be shipped on a truck

headlines.body: Nvidia announced Wednesday a new product that will put seven of its Vera Rubin AI racks into a shipping container, the company's latest effort to move up the stack and offer complete systems for artificial intelligence computing. The DSX Pod AI Factory is roughly the size of a standard shipping container and weighs about 28,000 kilograms (nearly 62,000 pounds), Nvidia said. It's designed to be shipped on a truck on normal roads and all the cabling and liquid cooling for the Pod are assembled at the factory, the company said. "The only thing that has to happen when it gets to the site is it's placed in its location, connected to the rest of the other containers, and validated through final burning and testing," Ian Buck, vice president of hyperscale computing at Nvidia, said on a call with reporters this week. The DSX Pod AI factory will reduce the time for a new AI data center to start serving tokens from six months to 14 days, according to the company. Nvidia said the pod is intended for customers worldwide and could help address deployment challenges faced by European customers. Nvidia did not announce a price for the system, but analysts say a single Vera Rubin rack can cost more than $7 million. The DSX Pod is a reference design that will ship from Nvidia's manufacturing partners. Nvidia said it was working with manufacturers including Foxconn, Gigabyte, Lenovo, HPE, Quanta and Pegatron. Nvidia expects deliveries to start in early 2027. Nvidia, once a chip company, now offers networking, storage and other data center needs to its customers. Its AI systems have evolved from single graphics processing unit chips to servers with four or eight GPUs, then to entire racks and now to the DSX Pod, a containerized building block with several racks already integrated. "What we offer into one gigawatt went from about $18 billion or so per gigawatt, to $20-something billion per gigawatt, to now $40-plus billion per gigawatt," Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said recently on a podcast. Gigawatts refer to the size of data center infrastructure by how much power is used. "My sense is that's going to keep going up."

headlines.body: Introducing NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture, an open hardware and software architecture for securing autonomous AI agents across the full stack. As agents take on long-running workflows at scale, safety requires controls outside the agents themselves. See why model alignment alone is not enough—and how models, tools, harnesses, and runtimes fit together. Without proper governance, agents can expose sensitive information, access unauthorized systems, or attempt to change their own permissions to complete a task. With models running on GPUs and harnesses and tools on CPUs, securing agents requires a systems approach. 📖 Read the press release → https://nvda.ws/4jzEjGv #NVIDIAGTC #AgenticAI #AISecurity #AISafety

headlines.body: Singapore's SC Capital Partners Group has invested in a data center project in South Korea. Set to offer 40MW of gross power capacity, the data center will be located in Pohang and is being developed in partnership with neocloud startup NeoAI Cloud. SC Capital Partners has not disclosed how much it has invested in the project. The data center project has also secured investment from government-backed capital. According to the companies, thus far the data center has received power approval, building permits, and construction has begun on the site. It is currently targeting completion by the end of 2027, and will be designed to support AI workloads, including liquid-cooled infrastructure ready for Nvidia Vera Rubin systems. The first phase will span 100,000 sqm (1 million sq ft). As of July of this year, around 2 trillion won ($1.35 billion) had been invested in the project. The site will be NeoAI's first data center, and the company will initially offer colocation services from the site. Jonathan Yongwan Jo, CEO of NeoAI Cloud, said: “We are pleased to secure this investment from SC Capital Partners, a leading investment firm in Asia Pacific real estate and digital infrastructure. The Pohang AI data center is envisioned to go beyond traditional colocation by leveraging high-density infrastructure space integrated with GPUaaS (GPU-as-a-Service) and AI platform capabilities to provide a high-performance foundation for global enterprises to develop AI models and operate services. Building on the successful delivery of this initial 40MW phase, we plan to advance a second phase expansion of 260MW and look forward to a continued partnership with SC Capital Partners.” Suchad Chiaranussati, chairman and founder of SC Capital Partners, added: “We are excited to complete this investment, which represents our continued expansion into digital infrastructure in Asia Pacific. The development benefits from strong underlying fundamentals and is well positioned to serve the evolving requirements of the digital economy. We remain focused on identifying high-quality opportunities, particularly in South Korea, where strong policy support for AI and digital infrastructure is contributing to a favorable environment for the sector, and working with experienced local partners to deliver investments that create long-term value for our investors.” Singaporean real estate investment firm SC Capital Partners has a data center company of its own called Zeus, which it launched in 2023 as a joint venture with Abner Investments. In August of this year, the company signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with SB Telecom Singapore – a subsidiary of SoftBank - and Malaysian IT consultant Robust HPC to build data centers in Southeast Asia. Pohang is a city on South Korea’s southeastern coast located in Gyeongsang Province. It is not a major data center hub. Huang Takes the Stage Huang opened with a question: What do L’Oréal, Revolut, Spotify, Merck, Vodafone, Zara, Porsche, Nestlé and HSBC have in common? They’re all European companies and they’re all working with NVIDIA on AI, he said. headlines.body: NVIDIA cuDSS, launched today in general availability, is an NVIDIA CUDA-X library that shifts a critical part of engineering and scientific simulations onto GPUs. Complex engineering feats — from advanced chips to aircraft to industrial systems —– depend on simulation to predict how designs will perform before they’re built. As designs become more complex, simulations take longer to run, increasing computing demands and limiting the number of ideas teams can test. NVIDIA cuDSS accelerates solving large sparse systems — the math-heavy step that repeats throughout engineering and scientific simulations and often limits how many designs a team can test — by tapping into GPUs. This lets applications reduce time to results and increase simulation throughput, enabling end users to explore larger more realistic models, more accurate representations and a wider design space at a reduced cost. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Industry leaders are already integrating NVIDIA cuDSS into their tools to transform workflows for their end customers: Applied Materials: With cuDSS, Applied Materials accelerated sparse solves in Ginestra, its physics-based, defect-centric simulation platform, by up to 10x versus CPU-only approaches, speeding exploration of semiconductor materials and device reliability. COMSOL: Using COMSOL Multiphysics with NVIDIA cuDSS on NVIDIA accelerated computing, ZEISS SMT achieved a measured 4x speedup in an EUV lithography plasma simulation benchmark, completing the full simulation in six days and 14 hours. Cadence : Uses cuDSS in its Celsius software to accelerate simulations of heat, structural stress and warpage in advanced chips and 3D chip designs, helping customers including Nokia analyze complex designs faster. Dassault Systèmes : Dassault Systèmes reports an 8-10x speedup using cuDSS within its Abaqus structural and computer simulation technology electromagnetic solvers for performance-critical simulations across industries. Siemens : Siemens uses cuDSS in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to accelerate simulations of structures in fluid-structure interaction workflows. Synopsys : Synopsys uses cuDSS in its Sentaurus Device simulator tool to accelerate simulations of advanced logic, memory and power chips, helping Infineon model increasingly complex devices faster. Accelerated Simulation at Scale As simulation workloads grow in size and complexity, cuDSS can scale out of the box from individual workstations to large computing clusters. Developers can integrate cuDSS into existing engineering, scientific and optimization software offerings, bringing GPU acceleration to tools already used by engineers and researchers. They can use cuDSS through C, C++, Python and Fortran interfaces. Learn more about cuDSS by visiting the NVIDIA demo booth and Dassault Systèmes booth at GTC Berlin. headlines.body: SSD controller designer FADU’s new File-Semantic SSD (FS-SSD) was announced at the 2026 OCP Global Summit. The new device promises to move the file system into the SSD itself. As detailed in a white paper , this enables GPUs, DPUs, and NICs to open and read files with “no host filesystem, no block layer, and no storage-server CPU in the path.” FADU told Tom’s Hardware Premium it expects partner samples by Q3 2027. FADU is a Seoul, South Korea-based fabless SSD controller designer . Its FS-SSD technology is designed to handle and improve the control path, as the data path side moved to accelerators years ago. FADU’s measurements show that the file system, plus block layers, can consume about 30% of CPU cycles in a GPUDirect Storage (GDS) random-read workload. It notes that bypass options give up the files, and the company claims its solution promises the best of both worlds. In FADU’s own preliminary Network File System (NFS) over NVMe test, on a drive built on its FC6161 Gen6 controller in a PCIe 5.0 host, remote file throughput held steady as the server downshifted from what FADU labels 16 cores to just one, maintaining about 460,000 ops/s. The NFSv3 operations are carried inside standard NVMe commands, and the drive handles path lookup, access control, and file-to-flash mapping. FS-SSD’s performance is remarkable when compared to Linux NFS-over-RDMA, which achieved a third of the ops/s with 16 cores and only 40K ops/s with one core. The technology remains “under active development,” and FADU told Tom’s Hardware Premium it expects Gen6-host results by Q1 2027, with partner samples in Q3 2027. FS-SSD holds about 460,000 ops/s from 16 server cores down to one, while NFS over RDMA falls from approximately 150,000 to 40,000 ops/s (Image credit: FADU ) FADU chooses to use NFSv3 because it’s “small (21 operations), OS- and filesystem-agnostic, and stateless” with low firmware overhead. FS-SSD supports PCIe today, with NVMe-oF over RDMA and TCP working without any new transport needed. Reusing an existing protocol is a smart move, in our view. Under the hood, the file system and flash translation layer are merged with a file layer derived from F2FS. Node and data blocks are aligned with the natural flash pages, sections at corresponding erase units, so that the F2FS node table becomes a “File Map” pointing the node IDs at physical flash addresses. One big advantage is that the DRAM mapping metadata overhead is considerably smaller: it uses the same amount of DRAM as a standard SSD, ~0.1% of NAND capacity (about 1 GB per TB), which a standard SSD fills almost entirely with its mapping table. Here, most of that DRAM, ~95%, can act as a hot-path node cache. One garbage collector also replaces two, avoiding what FADU calls the “double GC” of host F2FS, where file-system cleanup and the drive’s own garbage collection amplify each other. headlines.body: Neocloud Crusoe has developed a liquid-cooled version of its modular data center offering, Crusoe Spark. Crusoe Spark Liquid supports up to 3.5MW of compute per system, but can be deployed in multiple units up to 100MW, cofounder Cully Cavness told DCD. Production is expected to begin next year, from the company's existing factory in Brighton, Colorado. "It's a five-fold increase in computing density, going from 500kW IT in the [existing] air-cooled Spark version to now 3.5MW IT in the liquid-cooled Spark," Cavness, company president and chief strategy officer, said. The Spark uses closed-loop cooling, so will not consume any additional water beyond the initial filling phase. Each Spark consists of three shipping-container-sized modules "snapped together," Cavness said. "You can think of it in that form factor at roughly 60 feet long by 50 feet wide," he said, "that's a significant amount of space for things like compute, storage, networking, and we've designed it in a way that there's some flexibility so that over time, you can mix in next generations of chips and what might happen with storage and compute densities." Currently, the product is firmly aimed at Nvidia's latest GPUs - supporting Nvidia GB300 NVL72 and Vera Rubin NVL72 racks - with all the Spark Liquids set to be produced in 2027 expected to use Nvidia hardware. "Spark Liquid is one of the first designs that's compliant with DSX Modular," Cavness said, referring to Nvidia's new reference design for modular data centers. "They're also announcing that Spark is the first and only modular data center platform to achieve what they call Nvidia Exemplar status for cloud reliability. "They've done a bunch of testing on the way we interconnect different Sparks, and they've said that B300s perform in that deployment to the same level of speed and reliability as they do in a large stick-built traditional data center market." While the company believes that the performance is comparable, it still expects to take the traditional approach for larger-scale builds. "Ultimately, if you're going to go train a frontier model, we think still the large interconnected campus, like our flagship project in Abilene, probably makes sense if you're going toward gigawatt scale. headlines.body: BT has announced that its 5G Standalone (or 5G+ as the carrier calls it) network has extended to more than 80 percent of the UK population. The coverage update comes just over two years after EE launched its 5G SA network in the UK. While the 5G SA network has expanded in the UK to more locations, including Bicester, Chester, Durham, Portrush, and more, BT also revealed that it's aiming to bolster this even further with plans to trial AI-RAN on EE’s live network next year. It would be the first time the carrier has trialed the technology, on which it will be working with AI-RAN pioneers Nvidia and Nokia. Finnish vendor Nokia and GPU giant Nvidia first penned an agreement to develop AI-ready RAN solutions back in 2024, long before Nvidia became an investor in the vendor. These trials, set to take place in Birmingham, England, next year, will assess how AI could make mobile networks more responsive to customers' needs. The trials will take the technology from lab testing to EE's live network, noted BT, which said if the trial is successful, AI-RAN could help provide faster data speeds, more consistent connections, and allow the network to respond more intelligently as customer demand changes. “We’re seeing real momentum behind 5G+ as we progress towards our goal of 99 percent population coverage by 2030 – both in the pace of our rollout and in the amount of data customers are now using over the network. But reaching more people is only part of the story. We’re continuing to invest in making the network smarter and more responsive too, exploring technologies such as AI-RAN that could help us stay ahead of growing demand and deliver an even better experience for customers," said Greg McCall, chief security and networks officer, BT Group. Today's announcement coincides with Nvidia's GTC event in Berlin this week (which is being covered by both DCD and SDx Central), with Nokia confirming that French telco Orange plans to progress on testing AI-RAN in both lab and real network conditions, while Deutsche Telekom and Finland's Elisa have also logged progress on trials. EE said it's also increasing the capacity on its mobile network, which includes the delivery of its first 2.8Gbps microwave link, 40 percent more capacity than its previous 2Gbps benchmark.

releases.body: CuTe DSL Bug fixes and improvements: Fixed an issue with cute.extern where functions with zero arguments would generate invalid type signatures. Compiling such functions a second time would fail. Clear error/warning are now emitted for CopyUniversalOp with memory attributes specified ( !3711 ). CUTLASS Primitives' tensormap_replace now keeps device-side TMA descriptor updates safe when a descriptor is shrunk below its original extent (e.g. grouped GEMM) and fixes a possible illegal memory access on Blackwell/Rubin. This behavior can be opted out by specifying keep_oob_fetch_window=True . See https://docs.nvidia.com/datacenter/tesla/tesla-release-notes-595-91-07/index.html#known-issues for more details on the known cuTensorMapEncodeTiled bug. Fixed unintended sys.path modification that could break imports in some environments where Torch was not installed e.g. JAX. Known issues Due to a bug in CTK, the use of some packed instructions result in invalid code generation. Given the nature of the instructions and how they are explicitly used, we have chosen to not silently rewrite these, but rather are flagging until the upstream compiler fixes are available. Avoid packed higher-throughput FP8 (MMA_K=128) subtraction via inline PTX sub.rn.e4m3x4.e4m3x4 or sub.rn.e5m2x4.e5m2x4 , as incorrect code generation can produce wrong results. Some CUTLASS Primitives packed mixed-input ops compile incorrectly on Rubin (sm107a/sm107f), resulting in wrong code generation. README:  # Nemotron 3.5 Parse ### Description: Nemotron 3.5 Parse is a document image parser that produces structured, machine-readable text with semantic layout classes, bounding boxes, and reading order. It combines a C-RADIOv4-SO400M vision encoder with a 10-layer mBART decoder that consumes the visual sequence as a causal prefix. The release uses dynamic rectangular NaViT preprocessing, content-normalized coordinates, grouped-query self-attention (16 query heads and 8 key/value heads), a 72,505-token multilingual tokenizer, and chart-aware output through the ` ` token. It is intended for document understanding, information retrieval, data extraction, and multimodal data-curation workflows. Nemotron 3.5 Parse was developed by NVIDIA as a part of Nemotron. README:  **NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Embed**     # Nemotron-3.5-Embed-1B-NVFP4 Overview ## Description: **Nemotron-3.5-Embed-1B-NVFP4** is the quantized version of the [Nemotron-3.5-Embed-1B-BF16](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-3.5-Embed-1B-BF16) model, developed for multimodal and multilingual question-answering retrieval. The model can embed document pages in the form of image, text, or combined image–text inputs. Documents can be retrieved given a user query in text form. The model supports page images containing text, tables, charts, and infographics. The model is quantized with NVIDIA Model Optimizer, using nvidia-modelopt v0.47.0. For text retrieval, the model was evaluated across 34 languages: English, Arabic, Assamese, Bengali, Bulgarian, Chinese, Danish, Dutch, Finnish, French, German, Hindi, Hinglish, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Malay, Marathi, Nepali, Norwegian, Persian, Portuguese, Romanian, Russian, Spanish, Swahili, Swedish, Tamil, Telugu, Thai, Ukrainian, Urdu, and Vietnamese. For image retrieval, it was evaluated across 18 languages: Arabic, Bengali, Chinese, English, Persian, Finnish, French, German, Hindi, Indonesian, Japanese, Korean, Russian, Spanish, Swahili, Telugu, Thai, and Yoruba. The model may support additional languages beyond these evaluation sets. Read more details about Nemotron-3.5-Embed-1B-NVFP4 and other models in the family in our [Blog Post](https://huggingface.co/blog/nvidia/nemotron-retriever-world-class-agentic-retrieval).
